title: Deepak Fertilisers & Petrochemicals Corporation Ltd - 500645 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Deepak Fertilisers FY26 revenue rose about 12% to INR11,506 crores, but Q4 EBITDA fell to INR354 crores on input-cost inflation and a planned ammonia shutdown.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR3,011 crores and full-year EBITDA was INR1,684 crores, with full-year PAT of INR739 crores (down about 18% after adjusting for last year's one-time tax credit). Management described a strong first half and a weaker second half, driven by phos acid and sulfur cost spikes, lagging fertiliser subsidy pass-through, IPA price pressure, and a roughly INR75 crore one-off from the ammonia plant shutdown. Management said underlying trends are stabilising, with Mining Chemicals volumes up 12% YoY in Q4. Both growth projects (Gopalpur TAN and Dahej nitric acid) are targeted for commissioning in Q2 FY27, and the first LNG cargo under the 15-year Equinor contract arrived in May.

financial_highlights.change: sequential recovery in Industrial Chemicals; YoY not stated
includes about INR75 crore one-off from planned ammonia shutdown
about -18% YoY after adjusting prior-year one-time tax credit

segments.name: Mining Chemicals (TAN and explosives)
segments.commentary: Q4 volumes rose 12% YoY and 27% QoQ, with FY26 volume growth about 11%, driven by mining companies' year-end production targets. B2C now contributes about 16% of revenue versus 13% last year.

segments.name: Industrial Chemicals (nitric acid, IPA)
segments.commentary: Nitric acid volumes grew healthily in FY26. IPA faced weak prices and limited RGP availability, though management said IPA prices are currently very high due to LPG/propylene shortages and supply is limited.

segments.name: Crop Nutrition (fertilisers)
segments.commentary: Quarter was challenging on lower farm-gate prices, elevated channel inventory, and sharp input cost increases (phos acid, sulfur) with lagging subsidy realignment. Specialty and Croptek products are about 33% of segment revenue, up from 30%.

guidance_outlook: Gopalpur TAN project about 95% complete and Dahej nitric acid about 86% complete; commissioning expected in Q2 FY27, within approved capex.
Gopalpur TAN utilisation expected at 90-95% on a TPD basis by end of FY27, with near-full utilisation from exit level in FY28.
Total project capex approx INR4,650 crores; about INR3,800 crores spent including GST and advances, leaving about INR800-1,000 crores for FY27 including maintenance. Capex normalises after FY27.
Management expects quality of earnings to improve from tighter global supply, Equinor gas cost advantage, and higher Specialty and B2C mix.
Working capital build from fertiliser channel inventory expected to unwind in the next one to two months as kharif demand starts.
No debt number guided for FY27; the company will balance it once both projects are funded.
Demerger or subsidiary listing: no timeline yet; decision on form and timing pending.
capex_capacity: Gopalpur TAN facility about 95% complete; cumulative CWIP on both projects about INR3,050 crores; total cumulative spend including GST and advances about INR3,800 crores.
Dahej nitric acid project about 86% complete; commissioning expected Q2 FY27 after a one-quarter slip caused by skilled manpower shortages.
Ammonia plant had a planned shutdown in Q4 for efficiency and capacity improvements; management says capacity and efficiency have improved since.
Ammonia production at PCL about 500,000 tonnes per year (roughly 125,000 tonnes per quarter, per analyst question); company also trades large ammonia volumes.
Chardham Chemicals acquisition (about INR120 crores for 100% stake) has no revenue yet; revamp planned with no large capex expected.
Acquired an explosives unit (DMSL integration); DMSL CCDs of INR800 crores issued last year (INR500 crores third party, INR300 crores promoter entity), conversion around 30 months out.
demand_pricing: FGAN (ammonium nitrate) international prices firming, with March FOB around $300-400/t and further firming in Q1 FY27; domestic realisations are following.

IPA prices are very high, driven by LPG/propylene shortages cutting polypropylene output; management says prices will stay elevated for some time, with a new normal unlikely to return to earlier levels.
Ammonia prices are elevated; last published Middle East FOB around $800/t, and the analyst's domestic estimate was $900-1,000/t.
Fertiliser premiums on NPK were capped by government price controls ahead of state elections; subsidy support was inadequate against raw material inflation.
Q2 is seasonally weak for TAN due to monsoon, but management sees no long-term demand destruction.
Russia lifted its ammonium nitrate export ban in May 2026; supplies may resume at different price levels. India's export ban on ammonium nitrate was temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 TAN volume a new run rate, or was there backlog?
qa_highlights.answer: Tarun Sinha attributed higher Q4 volumes to mining companies' year-end production targets lifting explosives demand; Q2 is seasonally weaker, but no long-term demand destruction is seen. Current volumes come from existing capacity.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Equinor gas supply is secured, and for how long?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gas is fully secured: a minimum take-or-pay contract with the existing local supplier plus the 15-year Equinor contract, with further cargoes lined up every few months.

qa_highlights.question: Ammonia spread and margin uplift from gas contract?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify but said chemicals margins will improve holistically; the benefit flows through PCL. Partial reflection expected in the next quarter's results. An analyst estimate of INR450-500 crores quarterly EBITDA from ammonia was not confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further delays to Gopalpur and Dahej?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no further delay is expected; the Q1 to Q2 slip was due to skilled workforce shortages, with no other constraints visible.

qa_highlights.question: Dahej and Gopalpur ammonia supply tie-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it already imports and trades large ammonia volumes and has contracts with several suppliers on continuous monthly purchases; no long-term contract yet, but one can be signed as commissioning nears.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital build-up in fertilisers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed higher receivables and inventory to soft rabi demand and elevated trade channel inventory; expects normalisation within one to two months as kharif pull starts.

risks_watch: Commissioning slip risk for Gopalpur TAN and Dahej nitric acid (already slipped twice; skilled manpower shortage cited).
Net debt of INR4,824 crores and 2.86x net debt/EBITDA; management declined to guide FY27 debt.
Fertiliser working capital and channel inventory build-up; receivable and inventory days rose significantly in FY26.
Gas and ammonia procurement: landed costs are higher as refineries far away supply LPG/propylene; Hormuz-related procurement risk raised by an analyst.
Subsidy realignment lag and government price caps on NPK premiums.
El Nino impact on rainfall in crop geographies (management said impact could be lower but awaits detailed reports).
Chardham Chemicals revamp timeline and returns are undefined; no revenue yet.
Coal India developing its own ammonium nitrate capacity (a competitive risk for TAN).
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term value-chain story (LNG, ammonia, downstream, Gopalpur) but cautious and sometimes evasive on numbers: management declined to quantify the gas-contract benefit, ammonia margins, FY27 debt and Chardham valuation, citing that information is not yet public.
key_quotes: So as now we are seeing the real benefits emerging of our value chain, that is, LNG to ammonia to the complete downstream, that is now gradually coming alive.
Now we are fully secured. When I say fully secured, the way we have contract -- we have a minimum take-or-pay contract currently with our existing local supplier.
We expect by end of this year, we should be at least touching 90% to 95% utilization on a TPD basis.
No, definitely no. Even this quarter delay, which got delayed from Q4 to now -- or from Q1 to Q2 was not led by any major factor.

growth.why: Management guides Gopalpur TAN and Dahej nitric acid commissioning in Q2 FY27 within approved capex (about INR4,650 crore total, ~INR3,800 crore spent), with Gopalpur TAN utilisation targeted at 90-95% by end FY27; FY26 revenue grew about 12% but Q4 EBITDA fell and no explicit FY27 revenue growth number was given.
